what: The setups the diagnosis planner proposes for one model, with the reason for each, before and after rule set v5. Computed by calling the planner (optimizer.CatalogSource.Propose) with the request `tools/poc-modal/poc_modal.py` sends through `infercrane optimize propose --diagnosis-endpoint`. No GPU and no endpoint were involved.
limits: The diagnoses are constructed (a decode-bound window at a stated number of running requests), not measured on a server; a real endpoint's diagnosis decides which case applies.
A plan orders what to measure. Priority and expected benefit are planning priors, never a measured or predicted gain.
The plans say nothing about whether a setup starts or is faster; that is what a campaign measures.

before.finding: No speculation setup at 12 or 32 running requests, with or without the model config. Only the low-concurrency finding (at most 4 running requests per server) chose speculation; it was skipped unless the caller passed --model-config, because --allow-model-metadata-network was ignored together with --diagnosis-endpoint; and the derived setup drafted 1 token, not the publisher's 3.

decode_bound_32_running_6000_token_promp: fp8-weights (60): skipped, the weights already look quantized
decode_bound_12_running_6000_token_promp: fp8-weights (60): skipped, the weights already look quantized
low_concurrency_4_running: speculative-mtp (90): skipped as the harness asked (config not read); with the config declared, --speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}

after.finding: With the model config read (the harness now passes --allow-model-metadata-network), every decode-bound case proposes exactly the publisher's documented speculation option. It ranks first up to 16 running requests per server and after the FP8 KV cache above that on prompts of 7,000 tokens or more.

known_misses: "Larger batches" derives --max-num-seqs 2048 on an H100. vLLM 0.22.1 cannot start this model with more than 818 requests at once on one H100 (48 of its 64 layers keep a recurrent state per running request). The planner reads no per-model limit on requests at once, so it still proposes the setup; the harness skips it and records why. Not fixed here.
The planner's starting setup is the engine's defaults, not the endpoint's own command; the harness applies each proposed change to the publisher's command.
The publisher also documents two external drafters (DFlash2, DSpark). The planner has no reviewed draft model for this model and records speculative-draft-model as skipped.
